title: Al-Burooj 85:5-8 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: At-Tariq 9 to 17, Al-Burooj 1 to 11 and stopping signs
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 37 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Burooj 85:5-8 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 37. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: ٱلنَّارِ ذَاتِ ٱلْوَقُودِ (٥) إِذْ هُمْ عَلَيْهَا قُعُودٌۭ (٦) وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَفْعَلُونَ بِٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ شُهُودٌۭ (٧) وَمَا نَقَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَمِيدِ (٨)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: When they were sitting near it
And they, to what they were doing against the believers, were witnesses.
And they resented them not except because they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy,

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Clear meem; four or five counts
Idgham with ghunnah: noon into ي

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Burooj 85:5-8 together, ayah by ayah.
questions.a: The class recites 85:5-8 together without the mushaf.

questions.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 85:5-8 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Name the two names of Allah in 85:8.
questions.a: Al-'Aziz (the Exalted in Might) and Al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy).

questions.q: Why is «أَن يُؤْمِنُوا۟» read with ghunnah?
questions.a: Noon sakinah before ي is idgham with ghunnah.

options: Only because they believed in Allah
questions.a: A) Only because they believed in Allah. 85:8.

questions.q: Al-Burooj 85:7: «وَهُمْ عَلَىٰ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: The believers in Al-Burooj were harmed only because they believed in Allah (85:8). What gives a person courage to stay firm?
questions.a: Strong iman, knowing Allah is the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, and that His reward is greater than any harm.
